output.name: Ulsena
output.myth: Ulsena was a kelp-woman who lived in the cold shallows. One hot, calm day, which never comes here, she climbed onto the rocks and married Ristan, a fisherman of the north skerry. The next spring Tavo came laughing across the water and took his boat. Ulsena waited in the shallows. When no boat came back she did what kelp does when it wants the light. She grew. Her stalk went up past the seals and the gulls, and when it left the water it kept going, because Aun had cut the string. Now her bulb hangs in the Unflown, a hand-span west of the kite a mother ties for her drowned child. Varo, the grey boatman thin as a gutting knife, ferries the drowned across the dark to the south-west for a shell coin, and Ulsena has none, so she stays and looks. Her long brown fronds still sway. Mother Hesk counts her turns and says she has not yet found him. Sailors say that on a calm night, if you hear a slow creak over the water, it is Ulsena, still looking.
output.finding: Sailors far south, once you have found the Kite for the Drowned Child, look a hand-span to its west for the Kelp Bride's bulb, since the Unflown is never seen from the islands.
